title: Adapter manifest
description: Everything the platform knows about one tool. This is the single source: the HTTP endpoint, the MCP tool definition and the UI form are all projections of it, generated and never hand-maintained in parallel. JSON rather than YAML so it validates directly, needs no parser dependency, and is emitted reliably by a coding agent later.

version.description: Version of the wrapped tool, not of this manifest.

image.description: Container reference. A tag is tolerated while iterating; the conformance suite warns until it is pinned by digest, because an unpinned image makes every golden test a lie.

measured.description: Filled in by the profiler (P1), not by hand and not by guesswork. The conformance suite checks the declared class can actually hold these numbers. Absent until measured - an empty field is honest, an invented one is not.

fixture.description: Which fixture produced this. A tiny fixture profiles as nano and then falls over on a real genome.

datasets.description: Versioned reference data mounted read-only at run time. Never baked into the image, never downloaded per run - that is what turns a three-second tool into a forty-minute one.

operations.description: One tool, many operations. seqkit alone justifies this shape.

command.description: argv, never a shell string. Placeholders {{inputs.NAME}} and {{outputs.NAME}} are substituted with container paths. No shell means no quoting bugs and no injection surface.

stdin.description: Input port name to stream on stdin, for tools that accept nothing else.

stdout.description: Output port name to capture from stdout, for tools that write results there. Mutually exclusive with that port having a file path.

normalize.description: Applied to text outputs before golden comparison. Declared here rather than hardcoded in the runner, because which lines are noise is a fact about the tool. Many tools embed a timestamp or the full command line in their output; without this, every golden test rots overnight.

drop_lines.description: Regexes; matching lines are removed before comparison.

source.description: Where this tool actually came from. `homepage` is for humans; this is the evidence trail - what an agent read, what it built, and from which commit. Without it a manifest cannot be re-derived or audited, and 'the agent set it up' is unfalsifiable.

ref.description: Tag, branch or commit the adapter was derived from.

image_origin.description: Whether the image was pulled ready-made or built here. Decides who is responsible for rebuilding it.

dockerfile.description: Path to the Dockerfile, when built here.

provenance.description: Who or what produced this adapter, and how it was checked. Records that a machine wrote it and a human accepted it - the audit trail that makes eventual auto-merge defensible.

format.description: A format key within that type. Defaults to the type's first format.

alphabet.description: The residue alphabet this port carries, when it is fixed. Omit when the tool does not care.

alphabet_from.description: For an output whose alphabet is whatever went in. Names an input port. Most tools are pass-through - MAFFT aligns protein or DNA and emits whichever it was given - so a fixed alphabet would be a lie for them.

requires.description: Constraints this input places on whatever is wired to it. Only the facets named here are checked; everything else stays unconstrained, so an adapter that does not care needs no change.

alphabet.description: 'nucleotide' accepts dna or rna. This is the FastTree case: -nt is a nucleotide model and protein is wrong for it, but either nucleic acid is fine.

$comment: Everything the platform knows about one tool. Deliberately excluded: anything that accumulates at run time - last run, cost, failure rate, measured drift. Those belong in the catalogue record in Postgres, not here. A manifest is a declaration a human reviews and git tracks; if every run dirtied it, the diffs would stop being reviewable and the goldens would stop meaning anything.
